The rate has increased by **1 percentage point** (from 4% to 5%).

In relative terms, the increase is **25%**, because the 1-point rise is 25% of the original 4% rate: (5 − 4) ÷ 4 × 100 = 25%.
text:
Thank you for your question. To begin, the rate has increased by **1 percentage point**, moving from 4% to 5%. Put another way, the rate was 4% before the change and is 5% after it, so the difference between the two figures is one percentage point.

Turning to the relative change, the increase works out to **25%** when measured against the original figure. This is because the 1-point rise is 25% of the original 4% rate, which can be checked with the following calculation: (5 − 4) ÷ 4 × 100 = 25%.

I hope this explanation is helpful. Please let me know if you have any further questions.
